chunks.arabic_text: ١٣ - إبراهيم بن سليمان بن عبد الله بن حيان، الهمداني، الخزاز، النهمي، يكنى أبا إسحاق.

translations.en: 13 – Ibrāhīm b. Sulaymān b. ʿAbdullāh b. Hayyan, al-Hamdānī, al-Khazzāz, al-Nihmī, known by the kunya Abū Isḥāq.

chunks.arabic_text: يروي عن الضعفاء كثيرا. وفي مذهبه ضعف.

translations.en: He narrates from weak narrators a lot, and in his madhhab there is weakness.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights Ibrāhīm ibn Sulaym’s role as a transmitter who frequently relied on weaker sources, a practice that contributed to the criticism of his own reliability. The mention of 'weakness in his school of thought' (*fi madhhibihi*) suggests that his theological leanings, possibly distinct from the dominant Shia positions of the time, may have influenced the scholarly assessment of his narrations. This reflects the rigorous methodology of Shia hadith scholars in evaluating both the chain of transmission and the doctrinal consistency of narrators.
en.seo_question: Who is Ibrāhīm ibn Sulaym al-Hamdānī and what is his status in hadith sciences?
